properties.text: THE FIELD OF A BAR MAGNET -- forty compass needles, each one turned by the field where it stands, drawn by a single `repeat` block inside one Figure node.  MAGNET BEARING turns the bar and the whole field turns with it.  EARTH FIELD adds a uniform field up the page, which is what a real compass on a real table also feels: wind it up and the distant needles stop caring about the magnet and all point north.  Between those two regimes sit the NEUTRAL POINTS -- the places where the magnet's field exactly cancels the earth's -- and because each needle is drawn as long as the field it stands in, they show up as a limp pair that moves inwards as the earth field grows.  Set the earth field to 0 for the textbook bar-magnet plate on its own.

nodes.name: The field of a bar magnet

properties.program:
# THE FIELD OF A BAR MAGNET
# A grid of compass needles, each one turned by the field where it
# stands.  Nothing here is drawn twice: one `repeat` block places all
# forty of them.

view -62, -56, 62, 48

# --- the magnet ---------------------------------------------------
# bearing 0 points its north pole up the page; the poles sit at +/- d
# along that axis, and the whole field follows from the pair.
th = radians(bearing)
ux = sin(th)
uy = cos(th)

d  = 4.5
p  = 1000

# --- the needles --------------------------------------------------
# Eight columns and five rows.  The columns straddle the magnet --
# four to its left and four to its right, none on top of it -- so the
# middle row can run along the equator, which is where the interesting
# thing happens.
color "#303030"
width 0.25
repeat 40
    k  = i % 8
    gx = (12 + 12 * (k % 4)) * (2 * floor(k / 4) - 1)
    gy =  36 - 18 * floor(i / 8)

    # the field of two poles, each falling off as 1/r^2, plus the
    # earth's own field pointing up the page
    r1 = pow(hypot(gx - d * ux, gy - d * uy), 3)
    r2 = pow(hypot(gx + d * ux, gy + d * uy), 3)
    bx = p * (gx - d * ux) / r1 - p * (gx + d * ux) / r2
    by = p * (gy - d * uy) / r1 - p * (gy + d * uy) / r2 + earth

    # a needle is as long as the field is strong, so the places where
    # the two fields cancel show up as needles that have gone limp
    nl = clamp(4.2 * pow(hypot(bx, by) / 1.2, 0.25), 1.1, 3.8)
    nw = 0.34 * nl

    # drawn on axes turned to the field, so the needle lies along x:
    # the red half points north
    origin gx, gy, degrees(atan2(by, bx))
        poly  nl, 0, 0, nw, 0, -nw  with fill "#c03028"
        poly -nl, 0, 0, nw, 0, -nw  with fill "#e8e8e8"
    end
end

# --- the magnet itself, on top of the grid ------------------------
color "#202020"
width 0.6
# 12 long and 4.8 wide, drawn upright on axes turned clockwise by the
# bearing; the letters stay upright, only their anchors turn
origin 0, 0, -bearing
    rect -2.4, 0, 4.8,  6  with fill "#c03028"
    rect -2.4, 0, 4.8, -6  with fill "#e8e8e8"
    text 0,  3.3, "N"  with color "#ffffff"
    text 0, -3.3, "S"
end

# --- the labels ---------------------------------------------------
text 0, 47, "The field of a bar magnet"  with font 5.5, align "centre", "top"

font 3.8
align "left", "top"
text -58, -40, "bearing %.0f°      earth field %.2f", bearing, earth
text -58, -45, "each needle is as long as the field it stands in"
text -58, -50, "wind the earth field: the limp pair are the neutral points"
